senses.gloss: Sunlight and its warmth, thought of as something you sit in or keep out of.
examples: The kids were out in the *sun* all afternoon.
This corner of the yard gets very little *sun*.
Put a hat on and stay out of the *sun*.

senses.gloss: Help, encouragement, or money given to a person or a cause.
examples: Her family gave her a lot of *support* after the accident.
The bill has strong *support* in the Senate.
He pays child *support* every month.

senses.gloss: A part that holds the weight of something and keeps it from falling.
examples: Steel *supports* hold up the balcony.
The shelf needs another *support* in the middle.
Crews put temporary *supports* under the sagging roof.

senses.gloss: The way a situation looks from outside, as opposed to what is really going on.
examples: On the *surface*, the deal looks great.
Beneath the *surface*, the two sides still disagree.
Old tensions came to the *surface* during the meeting.

senses.gloss: A sudden large increase in something.
examples: The store saw a *surge* in sales before the holidays.
Hospitals prepared for a *surge* of new cases.
A *surge* in demand pushed prices up all spring.

senses.gloss: A strong forward rush of water, of a crowd, or of feeling.
examples: The storm *surge* flooded streets near the beach.
A *surge* of the crowd pushed him against the fence.
She felt a *surge* of pride watching her son graduate.

senses.gloss: A careful measurement of a piece of land and its exact boundaries.
examples: The bank required a *survey* before we closed on the house.
The *survey* showed the fence was two feet onto the neighbor's lot.
Crews finished the *survey* of the highway route last week.

senses.gloss: A general look at or review of a whole subject.
examples: The book is a *survey* of American art since 1945.
He took a quick *survey* of the damage after the storm.
Freshmen usually start with a *survey* course.

senses.gloss: An amount of food or drink taken down the throat at one time.
examples: He took a long *swallow* of coffee.
There were only a few *swallows* left in the bottle.
She washed the pill down with a *swallow* of water.

senses.gloss: Loose, soft cotton pants or a matching top worn for exercise or lounging.
examples: He came downstairs in a pair of gray *sweats*.
I live in *sweats* on the weekend.
Pack some *sweats* for the flight home.

senses.gloss: A single act of swinging your arm, a bat, or a club at something.
examples: He worked on his golf *swing* all summer.
She took a big *swing* and missed the ball.
The coach filmed each player's *swing* in slow motion.

senses.gloss: A clear shift from one position, mood, or result to another.
examples: There was a big *swing* toward the challenger in the final week.
Her mood *swings* worried her parents.
A ten-point *swing* in the polls decided the race.

senses.gloss: A sign that something is wrong in a situation or a system.
examples: Long lines at the airport are just a *symptom* of a bigger problem.
Rising rents are a *symptom* of the housing shortage.
The plan treats the *symptoms* of the crisis, not its causes.

senses.gloss: A thick sweet liquid medicine, especially one taken for a cough.
examples: Take two spoonfuls of cough *syrup* before bed.
The pharmacist recommended a *syrup* for younger kids.
She measured the *syrup* into the little plastic cup.

senses.gloss: The people and institutions in power, seen as a force that controls ordinary people.
examples: He says the whole *system* is rigged against small farmers.
You can't beat the *system*.
She spent years fighting the *system* to get her son help.

senses.gloss: A page open in a web browser, shown as a small labeled strip along the top.
examples: I had twenty *tabs* open and my laptop froze.
Open that link in a new *tab*.
Close the *tab* before you share your screen.

senses.gloss: A small flap or strip sticking out of something, used to pull it or label it.
examples: Pull the *tab* to open the box.
Each folder has a *tab* with the client's name on it.
The *tab* on the soda can broke off.

senses.gloss: A set of facts or numbers arranged in rows and columns.
examples: The report includes a *table* of monthly sales.
Check the *table* on page 12 for the exact figures.
She turned the raw data into a simple *table*.

senses.gloss: A flat, thin computer with a touchscreen and no attached keyboard.
examples: She reads the news on her *tablet* every morning.
The kids share a *tablet* for schoolwork.
My *tablet* needs charging again.

senses.gloss: A flat piece of stone or metal with words cut into it.
examples: The museum displays a clay *tablet* covered in ancient writing.
A bronze *tablet* by the door lists the building's donors.
The commandments were carved on stone *tablets*.

senses.gloss: A way of dealing with a problem; an approach.
examples: When arguing didn't work, she tried a different *tack*.
The company took a softer *tack* with unhappy customers.
That *tack* got us nowhere, so let's start over.

senses.gloss: The saddle, bridle, and other equipment used on a horse.
examples: She cleans her *tack* after every ride.
The barn has a room just for *tack*.
He bought a used saddle at the *tack* shop.

senses.gloss: A children's game in which one player chases the others and tries to touch one.
examples: The kids played *tag* in the backyard until dinner.
He's so fast that nobody can catch him at *tag*.
A game of *tag* broke out at recess.

senses.gloss: A word attached to a photo, post, or file so that it can be found later.
examples: Add a few *tags* so people can find the recipe.
The photo had my sister's name as a *tag*.
Search by *tag* instead of scrolling through everything.

senses.gloss: The money collected from a sale, a show, or a game.
examples: The night's *take* was over three thousand dollars.
They split the *take* evenly.
The movie's opening-weekend *take* surprised everyone.

senses.gloss: Formal discussions between two sides trying to reach an agreement.
examples: Peace *talks* resumed on Monday.
The two companies are in *talks* about a merger.
Contract *talks* broke down again last night.

senses.gloss: Rumor or gossip going around about someone or something.
examples: There's *talk* of layoffs in the spring.
Their new house is the *talk* of the neighborhood.
Don't pay attention to idle *talk*.

senses.gloss: A twisted, knotted mass of things such as wires, string, or branches.
examples: A *tangle* of cords sat behind the TV.
The trail disappeared into a *tangle* of vines.
She spent ten minutes undoing the *tangle* in her headphones.

senses.gloss: A large container for holding liquid or gas.
examples: The gas *tank* is almost empty.
We keep goldfish in a ten-gallon *tank*.
The water heater's *tank* sprang a leak.

senses.gloss: The practice of darkening your skin in the sun or under a lamp.
examples: She goes to a *tanning* salon before every vacation.
Doctors warn that *tanning* raises your risk of skin cancer.
He gave up *tanning* after a scare at the dermatologist.

senses.gloss: A light knock or touch with a finger or a foot.
examples: I felt a *tap* on my shoulder.
A double *tap* on the screen zooms in.
He gave the microphone a couple of *taps*.

senses.gloss: A device attached secretly to a phone line to listen in on calls.
examples: The FBI put a *tap* on his phone.
A judge approved the *tap* that week.
They found a *tap* on the office line.

senses.gloss: A result or figure that you are trying to reach.
examples: The team hit its sales *target* for the quarter.
The city set a *target* of 500 new apartments a year.
We're behind *target* on the fundraising.

senses.gloss: A person's sense of what is good or attractive in things like clothes, music, or art.
examples: She has excellent *taste* in furniture.
That joke was in poor *taste*.
His *tastes* run to old jazz records.

senses.gloss: A small wild duck of ponds and marshes, smaller than a mallard.
examples: A pair of *teal* landed on the far side of the pond.
Hunters were out before dawn looking for *teal*.
We counted a dozen *teal* along the shoreline.

senses.gloss: Temperature, in everyday informal speech.
examples: What's the *temp* outside?
Check the water *temp* before you get in.
The engine *temp* is running high again.

senses.gloss: A building where people gather to worship.
examples: They visited an ancient *temple* on the hillside.
Her family goes to *temple* on Friday nights.
The *temple* was rebuilt after the earthquake.

senses.gloss: A strip of chicken breast, usually breaded and fried.
examples: The kids ordered chicken *tenders* and fries.
He dipped a *tender* in honey mustard.
A basket of *tenders* comes with two sides.

senses.gloss: Money that must legally be accepted as payment.
examples: Every bill says it is legal *tender* for all debts, public and private.
Congress decides what counts as legal *tender*.
Old coins are still legal *tender* even if stores dislike them.

senses.gloss: The general meaning or mood of something said or written.
examples: The *tenor* of the meeting changed after she spoke.
I didn't catch every word, but I got the *tenor* of his remarks.
The *tenor* of the coverage has grown more critical.

senses.gloss: A permanent university position that protects a professor from being fired.
senses.ru: постоянная должность в вузе, бессрочный контракт
examples: She got *tenure* in her seventh year.
He was denied *tenure* and left for another school.
Fewer teaching jobs come with *tenure* these days.

senses.gloss: A flat step cut into a hillside for growing crops.
examples: Rice grows on *terraces* up the side of the valley.
The farmers cut *terraces* to keep the soil from washing away.
Each *terrace* is held in place by a low stone wall.

senses.gloss: The written words of a book, an article, or a document.
examples: The *text* of the speech was posted online that night.
The pictures are nice, but the *text* is hard to follow.
She compared the two *texts* line by line.

senses.gloss: A book used for study in a course.
examples: The required *texts* cost almost four hundred dollars.
He still has his old chemistry *text*.
The professor wrote the *text* we're using.

senses.gloss: The way a surface feels or looks when you touch it.
examples: The wall has a rough *texture*.
She likes fabrics with an interesting *texture*.
Sand the board until the *texture* is smooth.

senses.gloss: An improvement in relations between people or countries that had been unfriendly.
examples: The visit marked a *thaw* in relations between the two countries.
There's been a slight *thaw* between the brothers.
Trade talks brought a brief *thaw*.

senses.gloss: The art and business of writing and performing plays.
examples: She studied *theater* in college.
He has worked in *theater* for thirty years.
Community *theater* keeps the old playhouse busy.

senses.gloss: A large area where a war is being fought.
examples: He served in the Pacific *theater* during the war.
Supplies were flown into the *theater* every week.
Commanders in the *theater* asked for more troops.

senses.gloss: The main idea that runs through a book, a film, or a discussion.
examples: Loneliness is the main *theme* of the novel.
Several *themes* came up again and again in the interviews.
The *theme* of her talk was second chances.

senses.gloss: A tune played again and again in a film, a show, or a piece of music.
examples: Everyone recognizes the *theme* from that movie.
The show's opening *theme* is only fifteen seconds long.
He hummed the *theme* all the way home.

senses.gloss: Something a person owns; a personal belonging.
examples: Pack your *things* — we leave at six.
She left a few *things* at my apartment.
He put his *things* in a locker by the door.

senses.gloss: A strong wish for something.
examples: She has a real *thirst* for adventure.
His *thirst* for knowledge never faded.
There's a growing *thirst* for change in the district.

senses.gloss: The part of the human body between the neck and the abdomen; the chest.
examples: The X-ray showed a shadow in the *thorax*.
The surgeon opened the *thorax* to reach the heart.
Pain in the *thorax* should be checked right away.

senses.gloss: A fungal infection that leaves white patches in the mouth, common in babies.
examples: The baby has *thrush* and won't nurse.
The doctor prescribed drops for the *thrush*.
*Thrush* can pass back and forth between a nursing mother and her baby.

senses.gloss: The main point of what someone is saying.
examples: The *thrust* of her argument was that the plan costs too much.
I missed the details, but I got the general *thrust*.
That's the whole *thrust* of the report.

senses.gloss: A sudden strong push, especially with a weapon.
examples: He blocked the *thrust* with his shield.
One quick *thrust* of the shovel broke through the ice.
The fencer scored with a low *thrust*.

senses.gloss: The short sharp sound a clock makes.
examples: The only sound was the *tick* of the kitchen clock.
He counted the *ticks* while he waited.
The watch has a very quiet *tick*.
